# CBACT04C — Interest Calculator (Batch)

## Overview

CBACT04C is the monthly interest posting batch job for the CardDemo card-account system. It walks the transaction-category balance file (`TCATBALF`) in key order — one record per account / transaction-type / transaction-category combination — and for each balance it looks up the interest rate that applies to that account's disclosure group and category. Where a non-zero rate applies, it computes one month's interest on that category balance, accumulates it into a running per-account total, and writes a new system-generated interest transaction into the output transaction file (`TRANSACT`). When the account number changes (and again at end of file), it posts the accumulated interest to the account master record: the total interest is added to the current balance and both current-cycle credit and debit counters are reset to zero. The program also resolves the account's card number via the card cross-reference file so the generated transaction carries a card number, and it stamps each generated transaction with a DB2-format timestamp. A fee-computation step exists but is an empty stub.

## Paragraph flow

The `PROCEDURE DIVISION` receives `EXTERNAL-PARMS` (`PARM-LENGTH`, `PARM-DATE`) from the caller. The mainline displays a start banner, opens all five files, then loops `UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y'`:

- While not at end of file, it performs `1000-TCATBALF-GET-NEXT`. If that read did not hit end of file, it increments `WS-RECORD-COUNT`, displays the record, and checks whether `TRANCAT-ACCT-ID` differs from `WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM`.
- On an account break: if `WS-FIRST-TIME` is not `'Y'` it performs `1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT` for the *previous* account; otherwise it just sets `WS-FIRST-TIME` to `'N'`. Either way it then zeroes `WS-TOTAL-INT`, saves the new account id into `WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM` and into `FD-ACCT-ID`, performs `1100-GET-ACCT-DATA`, moves the account id into `FD-XREF-ACCT-ID`, and performs `1110-GET-XREF-DATA`.
- For every record (break or not) it builds the disclosure-group key from `ACCT-GROUP-ID`, `TRANCAT-CD` and `TRANCAT-TYPE-CD`, performs `1200-GET-INTEREST-RATE`, and — only `IF DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0` — performs `1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST` and then `1400-COMPUTE-FEES`.
- When the read sets `END-OF-FILE` to `'Y'`, the next pass through the loop takes the `ELSE` branch and performs `1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT` one final time, flushing the last account's accumulated interest.

After the loop it closes all five files, displays an end banner, and issues `GOBACK`.

### 0000-TCATBALF-OPEN
Sets `APPL-RESULT` to 8, opens `TCATBAL-FILE` for input. Status `'00'` sets `APPL-RESULT` to 0, anything else sets it to 12. If `APPL-AOK` (value 0) is not true, it displays `'ERROR OPENING TRANSACTION CATEGORY BALANCE'`, copies the file status into `IO-STATUS`, and calls `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` then `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 0100-XREFFILE-OPEN
Same pattern for `XREF-FILE` (`OPEN INPUT`). On failure it displays `'ERROR OPENING CROSS REF FILE'` together with `XREFFILE-STATUS`, then performs `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 0200-DISCGRP-OPEN
Same pattern for `DISCGRP-FILE` (`OPEN INPUT`). The failure message reads `'ERROR OPENING DALY REJECTS FILE'` — a copy-paste artifact; the file being opened is the disclosure-group file, not a rejects file. Calls `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM` on failure.

### 0300-ACCTFILE-OPEN
Opens `ACCOUNT-FILE` `I-O` (read/update), because the account master is rewritten in place later. Failure path displays `'ERROR OPENING ACCOUNT MASTER FILE'` and abends via the same two paragraphs.

### 0400-TRANFILE-OPEN
Opens `TRANSACT-FILE` `OUTPUT` — the transaction file is created fresh each run, so any prior content is replaced. Failure path displays `'ERROR OPENING TRANSACTION FILE'` and abends.

### 1000-TCATBALF-GET-NEXT
`READ TCATBAL-FILE INTO TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD` — a sequential read of the indexed balance file. Status `'00'` → `APPL-RESULT` 0; status `'10'` (end of file) → `APPL-RESULT` 16, which satisfies the `APPL-EOF` condition and moves `'Y'` to `END-OF-FILE`; any other status → `APPL-RESULT` 12, which displays `'ERROR READING TRANSACTION CATEGORY FILE'` and abends.

### 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT
Posts the accumulated interest to the account currently held in `ACCOUNT-RECORD`:

```
ADD WS-TOTAL-INT  TO ACCT-CURR-BAL
MOVE 0 TO ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT
MOVE 0 TO ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT
```

The running total interest is added to the account's current balance, and both current-cycle credit and debit totals are cleared to zero. It then does `REWRITE FD-ACCTFILE-REC FROM ACCOUNT-RECORD`; status other than `'00'` displays `'ERROR RE-WRITING ACCOUNT FILE'` and abends.

### 1100-GET-ACCT-DATA
Random-reads `ACCOUNT-FILE INTO ACCOUNT-RECORD` on the key `FD-ACCT-ID` (previously loaded with `TRANCAT-ACCT-ID`). The `INVALID KEY` clause displays `'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: '` with the key, but does not itself stop processing — the status check immediately after treats any status other than `'00'` as fatal, displaying `'ERROR READING ACCOUNT FILE'` and abending. So a missing account produces both messages and then an abend.

### 1110-GET-XREF-DATA
Random-reads `XREF-FILE INTO CARD-XREF-RECORD` using the alternate key `FD-XREF-ACCT-ID` to obtain `XREF-CARD-NUM` for the account. `INVALID KEY` displays `'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: '` with the account id; as above, any status other than `'00'` then displays `'ERROR READING XREF FILE'` and abends.

### 1200-GET-INTEREST-RATE
Random-reads `DISCGRP-FILE INTO DIS-GROUP-RECORD` on the key built from the account's group id, transaction type code and category code. `INVALID KEY` displays `'DISCLOSURE GROUP RECORD MISSING'` and `'TRY WITH DEFAULT GROUP CODE'`. Status `'00'` **or** `'23'` (record not found) is treated as acceptable (`APPL-RESULT` 0); anything else is fatal (`'ERROR READING DISCLOSURE GROUP FILE'`, then abend). When the status is `'23'`, it moves the literal `'DEFAULT'` into `FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID` and performs `1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE` to retry the lookup under the default group.

### 1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE
Re-reads `DISCGRP-FILE INTO DIS-GROUP-RECORD` with the `'DEFAULT'` group id in the key. Here only status `'00'` is acceptable — if the default disclosure-group record is also missing, it displays `'ERROR READING DEFAULT DISCLOSURE GROUP'` and abends.

### 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST
Computes one month's interest for the current category balance:

```
COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-INT
 = ( TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200
```

That is: the category balance multiplied by the annual percentage rate, divided by 1200 — dividing by 100 to convert the percentage and by 12 to reduce the annual rate to a monthly one. The result lands in `WS-MONTHLY-INT` (`S9(09)V99`), so it is truncated to two decimal places (no `ROUNDED` phrase is present). It then does `ADD WS-MONTHLY-INT TO WS-TOTAL-INT`, accumulating this category's interest into the per-account running total, and performs `1300-B-WRITE-TX`.

### 1300-B-WRITE-TX
Builds and writes one interest transaction record. It adds 1 to `WS-TRANID-SUFFIX` and builds the transaction id by `STRING`-ing `PARM-DATE` and `WS-TRANID-SUFFIX` `DELIMITED BY SIZE` into `TRAN-ID` — i.e. the 10-character run date passed in as a parameter followed by the 6-digit sequence number, filling the 16-byte id. It then populates the record: `TRAN-TYPE-CD` = `'01'`, `TRAN-CAT-CD` = `'05'`, `TRAN-SOURCE` = `'System'`, `TRAN-DESC` built by `STRING`-ing the literal `'Int. for a/c '` with `ACCT-ID`, `TRAN-AMT` = `WS-MONTHLY-INT`, `TRAN-MERCHANT-ID` = 0, merchant name/city/zip = spaces, and `TRAN-CARD-NUM` = `XREF-CARD-NUM` from the cross-reference read. It performs `Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP` and moves `DB2-FORMAT-TS` into both `TRAN-ORIG-TS` and `TRAN-PROC-TS`. Finally `WRITE FD-TRANFILE-REC FROM TRAN-RECORD`; any status other than `'00'` displays `'ERROR WRITING TRANSACTION RECORD'` and abends.

### 1400-COMPUTE-FEES
A stub. The body is only the comment `To be implemented` and `EXIT` — no fee logic exists. It is still performed once per non-zero-rate balance record, immediately after `1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST`.

### 9000-TCATBALF-CLOSE
Closes `TCATBAL-FILE`; status other than `'00'` displays `'ERROR CLOSING TRANSACTION BALANCE FILE'` and abends.

### 9100-XREFFILE-CLOSE
Closes `XREF-FILE`; failure displays `'ERROR CLOSING CROSS REF FILE'` and abends.

### 9200-DISCGRP-CLOSE
Closes `DISCGRP-FILE`; failure displays `'ERROR CLOSING DISCLOSURE GROUP FILE'` and abends.

### 9300-ACCTFILE-CLOSE
Closes `ACCOUNT-FILE`; failure displays `'ERROR CLOSING ACCOUNT FILE'` and abends.

### 9400-TRANFILE-CLOSE
Closes `TRANSACT-FILE`; failure displays `'ERROR CLOSING TRANSACTION FILE'` and abends.

### Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP
Reads the system clock with `MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO COBOL-TS`, then reassembles the pieces into a 26-character DB2-style timestamp string in `DB2-FORMAT-TS`: year, month, day, hour, minute, second and hundredths are moved across individually, `'0000'` is moved to the trailing `DB2-REST`, hyphens are placed in the three date separators and periods in the three time separators — producing the `YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.hh0000` layout described in the source comment. Called by `1300-B-WRITE-TX` before each transaction write.

### 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM
Displays `'ABENDING PROGRAM'`, sets `TIMING` to 0 and `ABCODE` to 999, then `CALL 'CEE3ABD' USING ABCODE, TIMING` — the Language Environment abend service. This terminates the job; there is no return path.

### 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS
Formats a file status for display. If `IO-STATUS` is not numeric or `IO-STAT1` is `'9'`, it treats the second byte as a binary value: it moves `IO-STAT1` into the first position of `IO-STATUS-04`, zeroes `TWO-BYTES-BINARY`, moves `IO-STAT2` into `TWO-BYTES-RIGHT` (the redefined low-order byte), moves `TWO-BYTES-BINARY` into `IO-STATUS-0403`, and displays `'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN'` with the result. Otherwise it moves `'0000'` into `IO-STATUS-04`, overlays positions 3–4 with the two status characters, and displays the same message. This is display-only; the abend decision is made by the caller.

## Business rules

- **Interest formula, verbatim:** `COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-INT = ( TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200`. The divisor is the literal 1200 (percent conversion × 12 months). Reproduce this exactly — do not restructure it as `rate/100/12` or apply rounding at an intermediate step.
- **Truncation, not rounding:** there is no `ROUNDED` phrase. `WS-MONTHLY-INT` is `S9(09)V99`, so the quotient is truncated toward zero at two decimal places. A Java implementation must truncate (`RoundingMode.DOWN`) to scale 2, not use half-up.
- **Zero rate skips everything:** interest is computed, accumulated and written only `IF DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0`. A zero rate produces no transaction record, no addition to `WS-TOTAL-INT`, and no fee call.
- **Disclosure-group fallback:** if the group/type/category lookup returns status `'23'` (not found), the group id is replaced with the literal `'DEFAULT'` and the lookup is retried. A miss on the *default* record is fatal and abends the program.
- **Account-break posting:** the account master is updated only when the account id changes, and the update applies to the *previous* account's accumulated total. `WS-FIRST-TIME` (initial value `'Y'`) suppresses the update on the very first record, since there is no previous account yet.
- **End-of-file flush:** after the read reports end of file, the loop makes one more pass and performs `1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT` so the final account's interest is posted. Omitting this final flush loses the last account's interest.
- **Account posting effect:** `ADD WS-TOTAL-INT TO ACCT-CURR-BAL`, then `ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT` and `ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT` are both set to zero. The cycle counters are cleared unconditionally as part of the same posting step.
- **Total reset order:** `WS-TOTAL-INT` is zeroed *after* the previous account's update and *before* reading the new account's data, so each account accumulates independently.
- **Generated transaction constants:** every generated record uses `TRAN-TYPE-CD` `'01'`, `TRAN-CAT-CD` `'05'`, `TRAN-SOURCE` `'System'`, `TRAN-MERCHANT-ID` 0, and blank merchant name/city/zip.
- **Transaction id construction:** `PARM-DATE` concatenated with `WS-TRANID-SUFFIX`, both `DELIMITED BY SIZE`, into the 16-byte `TRAN-ID`. The suffix is a run-global counter starting at 0 and incremented before each write — it is not reset per account.
- **Timestamps:** `TRAN-ORIG-TS` and `TRAN-PROC-TS` both receive the same `DB2-FORMAT-TS` value, captured freshly per transaction from the system clock.
- **Output file is replaced:** `TRANSACT-FILE` is opened `OUTPUT`, so each run creates the file anew rather than appending.
- **Any unexpected file status is fatal:** open, read (other than end of file), rewrite, write and close all treat a status other than `'00'` (plus `'23'` on the first disclosure-group read) as an abend with code 999 via `CEE3ABD`. There is no skip-and-continue error recovery anywhere in this program.
- **Fees are not implemented:** `1400-COMPUTE-FEES` is an empty stub. A faithful port should preserve it as an explicit no-op extension point rather than inventing fee logic.
- **`ACCT-GROUP-ID` persistence:** the disclosure key is rebuilt for every balance record from whatever `ACCOUNT-RECORD` currently holds — the account record read at the last account break — so all categories for an account share that account's group id.

*Observation for the human reviewer, not a correction:* `WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM` is mapped as `String` (`PIC X(11)`) while `TRANCAT-ACCT-ID` is `BigDecimal` (`PIC 9(11)`). The COBOL comparison `IF TRANCAT-ACCT-ID NOT= WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM` and the move between them rely on alphanumeric/numeric conversion semantics; a Java port needs a deliberate decision about how that comparison is expressed. The mapped shapes above stand as given.

## Flagged for human review

These fields were deliberately not mapped by the parser (per ADR-0002, `REDEFINES` routes to a human gate rather than being parsed). No Java shape is guessed for any of them.

- **`TWO-BYTES-LEFT`** — declared under `01 TWO-BYTES-ALPHA REDEFINES TWO-BYTES-BINARY`; overlays the high-order byte of a binary halfword, so its storage and Java shape depend on host byte order and cannot be derived from the `PIC X` clause alone.
- **`TWO-BYTES-RIGHT`** — same `REDEFINES` group; used in `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` to inject a single status byte into the low-order half of `TWO-BYTES-BINARY` and read it back as a number. This byte-reinterpretation trick has no direct Java equivalent and needs a human decision.
- **`DB2-YYYY`** — part of `01 FILLER REDEFINES DB2-FORMAT-TS`, an overlay carving the 26-byte timestamp string into positioned subfields.
- **`DB2-MIN`** — same `REDEFINES` overlay on `DB2-FORMAT-TS`.
- **`DB2-DOT-2`** — same `REDEFINES` overlay; a separator character position within the timestamp.
- **`DB2-SS`** — same `REDEFINES` overlay on `DB2-FORMAT-TS`.
- **`DB2-DOT-3`** — same `REDEFINES` overlay; a separator character position within the timestamp.
- **`DB2-MIL`** — same `REDEFINES` overlay; note it is declared `PIC 9(002)` inside an otherwise alphanumeric overlay, which is exactly the kind of mixed-usage redefinition the ADR routes to a human.
- **`DB2-REST`** — same `REDEFINES` overlay; the trailing four positions set to the literal `'0000'`.

All nine flagged fields belong to just two `REDEFINES` groups: the binary/character overlay used for file-status display, and the timestamp-assembly overlay used by `Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP`. The remaining subfields of the timestamp overlay (`DB2-STREEP-1/2/3`, `DB2-MM`, `DB2-DD`, `DB2-HH`, `DB2-DOT-1`) appear in the same declaration and should be reviewed alongside these, as the whole overlay must be reimplemented as one unit — most naturally as timestamp formatting rather than as individual fields.

One further note on the source text: the `01 FILLER REDEFINES DB2-FORMAT-TS` declaration carries stray single characters (`E`, `-`, `M`, `-`, `D`, `-`, `U`) in the far-right comment columns of the timestamp subfield lines. These are annotation remnants marking the timestamp layout, not code, and they appear inside the flagged declaration snippets above.

rule_confidence.rule: Interest formula uses divisor 1200: `COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-INT = ( TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200`
rule_confidence.rationale: 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST contains this exact formula character-for-character, no variation.

rule_confidence.rule: No ROUNDED phrase; WS-MONTHLY-INT (S9(09)V99) truncates the quotient to two decimal places
rule_confidence.rationale: The COMPUTE statement in 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST carries no ROUNDED clause. The field definition confirms S9(09)V99.

rule_confidence.rule: Interest computation, accumulation, and transaction write are skipped if DIS-INT-RATE = 0
rule_confidence.rationale: Main loop explicitly wraps both 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST and 1400-COMPUTE-FEES in `IF DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0`.

rule_confidence.rule: On disclosure-group lookup status '23', retry with FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID set to literal 'DEFAULT'
rule_confidence.rationale: 1200-GET-INTEREST-RATE checks status '23' and moves 'DEFAULT' to FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID, then performs 1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE.

rule_confidence.rule: Account master update (1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT) is performed only on account break, not on first record
rule_confidence.rationale: Account-break logic in main loop: `IF WS-FIRST-TIME NOT = 'Y'` wraps the update call; first record sets flag to 'N' instead.

rule_confidence.rule: WS-TOTAL-INT is zeroed after previous account's update and before new account data is read
rule_confidence.rationale: Account-break sequence in main loop: update (if not first), then `MOVE 0 TO WS-TOTAL-INT`, then `PERFORM 1100-GET-ACCT-DATA`.

rule_confidence.rule: When EOF is detected, the loop executes one final account update before terminating
rule_confidence.rationale: The final update does occur: when 1000-TCATBALF-GET-NEXT sets END-OF-FILE = 'Y', the ELSE branch of the outer IF (not the 'next iteration') executes 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT. The spec's phrasing 'the next pass through the loop' is imprecise—the ELSE is taken in the same iteration, not after looping back—but the net claim (final account is updated after EOF) is correct.

rule_confidence.rule: Generated transactions all use TRAN-TYPE-CD='01', TRAN-CAT-CD='05', TRAN-SOURCE='System'
rule_confidence.rationale: 1300-B-WRITE-TX contains these exact moves: `MOVE '01' TO TRAN-TYPE-CD`, `MOVE '05' TO TRAN-CAT-CD`, `MOVE 'System' TO TRAN-SOURCE`.

rule_confidence.rule: Transaction ID is constructed by STRING-ing PARM-DATE and WS-TRANID-SUFFIX (both DELIMITED BY SIZE) into 16-byte TRAN-ID; suffix is global counter starting at 0, incremented before each write
rule_confidence.rationale: 1300-B-WRITE-TX: `ADD 1 TO WS-TRANID-SUFFIX` then STRING PARM-DATE, WS-TRANID-SUFFIX into TRAN-ID. WS-TRANID-SUFFIX is initialized `VALUE 0` and never reset per account.

rule_confidence.rule: TRAN-ORIG-TS and TRAN-PROC-TS both receive the same DB2-FORMAT-TS value, captured freshly per transaction
rule_confidence.rationale: 1300-B-WRITE-TX calls Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP (which reads CURRENT-DATE) then moves its result to both fields; the timestamp routine is called once per transaction write.

rule_confidence.rule: TRANSACT-FILE is opened OUTPUT, so each run replaces the file rather than appending
Any file status other than '00' (plus '23' on first disclosure-group read) causes abend via CEE3ABD with code 999
rule_confidence.rationale: All open/read/rewrite/write/close paths check status and call 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM on error; 1200-GET-INTEREST-RATE treats '00' OR '23' as acceptable, then 1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE enforces '00' only.

rule_confidence.rule: 1400-COMPUTE-FEES is an empty stub (comment 'To be implemented' and EXIT only)
rule_confidence.rationale: 1400-COMPUTE-FEES contains only a comment and EXIT.

rule_confidence.rule: Disclosure-group key is rebuilt from ACCT-GROUP-ID (read at account break) for every balance record
rule_confidence.rationale: Main loop moves ACCT-GROUP-ID to FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID for every record; ACCOUNT-RECORD is refreshed only at account breaks, so all categories per account use that account's group.

rule_confidence.rule: Both ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT and ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT are set to 0 as part of account posting (1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT)
rule_confidence.rationale: 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT: `MOVE 0 TO ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT` and `MOVE 0 TO ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT` executed unconditionally after the ADD.

rule_confidence.rule: DB2 timestamp format is YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.hh0000 (hyphens in date, periods in time, trailing 0000)
rule_confidence.rationale: Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP sets the three date separators (DB2-STREEP-1/2/3) to '-', the three time separators (DB2-DOT-1/2/3) to '.', and DB2-REST to '0000'; the redefined structure confirms 26 total characters with this layout.

rule_confidence.rule: 1100-GET-ACCT-DATA random-reads on key FD-ACCT-ID (implicitly, as primary key of ACCOUNT-FILE)
rule_confidence.rationale: 1100-GET-ACCT-DATA has no explicit KEY clause; ACCOUNT-FILE is defined with `RECORD KEY IS FD-ACCT-ID`, so the READ uses the primary key by default.

rule_confidence.rule: 1110-GET-XREF-DATA random-reads on alternate key FD-XREF-ACCT-ID (explicitly specified with KEY IS clause)
rule_confidence.rationale: 1110-GET-XREF-DATA contains `READ XREF-FILE... KEY IS FD-XREF-ACCT-ID`; XREF-FILE is defined with `ALTERNATE RECORD KEY IS FD-XREF-ACCT-ID`.

rule_confidence.rule: 0200-DISCGRP-OPEN displays error message 'ERROR OPENING DALY REJECTS FILE' (noted as copy-paste artifact)
rule_confidence.rationale: 0200-DISCGRP-OPEN displays exactly this text, and it is indeed incorrect (should reference disclosure-group file, not rejects). The spec correctly identifies this as an artifact.

steps.description: Opens the transaction-category balance, card cross-reference, disclosure-group, account master (I-O) and transaction output resources, abending the job on any status other than '00'.
Sequentially reads the next transaction-category balance record in key order, signalling end of file on status '10'.
On an account-number change, randomly reads the account master by account id and the card cross-reference by alternate account key, attaching both to the current category balance.
Looks up the disclosure-group record from the account's group id, transaction type and category code, retrying under the literal 'DEFAULT' group when the first read returns status '23'.
Computes ( TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200 truncated to two decimals as this category's monthly interest, which is later summed per account for posting.

Builds the system-generated interest transaction — id from PARM-DATE plus the run-global suffix, type '01', category '05', source 'System', amount WS-MONTHLY-INT, card number from the cross-reference, and both timestamps from the DB2-format clock value — for writing to the transaction file.
Explicit no-op extension point preserved from the empty COBOL fee stub, invoked once per non-zero-rate category balance and passing the item through unchanged.

Control-break owner for the per-account interest total: adds the accumulated interest to ACCT-CURR-BAL, zeroes ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT and ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT, and yields the account for rewrite (also flushed once after end of file).
Closes all five resources at end of run, abending on any close status other than '00'.

rest_endpoints.description: Launches the interest calculation batch job for a given run date parameter and returns the created job execution id.
Returns the status, timings and record counts of one interest calculation job execution.
Point query returning a single account master record, including its current balance and cycle credit/debit totals.
Point query returning the transaction-category balance rows currently held for one account.
Point query resolving the card cross-reference record (card and customer id) for one account.
Point query returning the disclosure-group interest rate for a group, transaction type and category combination.
Point query returning a single transaction record, including interest transactions generated by the batch run.
